title: Spot three samples on a TLC plate with glass capillaries and stand it in the developing tank
instruction: Counting from the robot's left, the first spotter goes with the first vial and the first mark on the baseline, the second with the second, the third with the third. Fill each spotter by dipping its tip in its vial, touch it once, briefly and lightly, to its mark, and return it to the rack. Then stand the plate in the developing tank, spotted face out, bottom edge in the solvent and baseline above it, leaning back against the back wall, and put the lid on.
context: Synthetic chemists check how a reaction is going by thin-layer chromatography, routinely and by hand (Nichols, Organic Chemistry Lab Techniques, 2.3E 'Step-by-Step Procedures for TLC'). Each sample is taken up in a glass capillary spotter and put on its pencil mark with a quick, light touch that leaves a spot about 2 mm across: a long touch makes a large spot, a hard one gouges the silica, and a sideways knock snaps the capillary. The plate, handled only by its edges, then stands in a covered chamber with the solvent below the baseline. Dyed water stands in for the samples and water for the eluent, so trials are safe to repeat; the manipulation is the same.
setup: Units mm. x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. Two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases at y = +305 and y = -305, ready pose, grippers open, each pad covered with a nitrile finger cot; one overhead camera and one on each wrist. Lab bench. (1) MilliporeSigma 1.15327 TLC plate, silica gel 60 F254 on glass, 25 x 75 mm, glass about 2 mm, lying silica up on a 76 mm length of 12.7 mm square aluminium bar (a riser, so the plate can be lifted by its edges only) centred at (262, 20), its long sides along x, its bottom edge toward the robot. A light pencil baseline 10 mm above the bottom edge carries three 2 mm pencil ticks 6 mm apart, marks 1 to 3 from the robot's left, at (235, 26), (235, 20) and (235, 14). (2) Three spotters: borosilicate capillaries 1.5 mm OD x 0.86 mm ID x 100 mm (Warner Instruments 30-0053, standard wall, no filament), empty, standing in 5 mm holes 20 mm deep in a 30 x 110 x 25 mm foam block at (165, 190), (165, 150), (165, 110): spotters 1 to 3 from the robot's left. (3) Three 4 mL glass vials (15 x 45 mm, open), each with 1 mL of water and two drops of food colouring (sample 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green; non-hazardous), in a 30 x 120 x 20 mm foam vial block with 16 mm through-holes at (235, 180), (235, 140), (235, 100). Spotter k, sample k and mark k belong together. (4) The developing chamber, a TLC chamber with a lid as in Nichols: a Sigma-Aldrich Z146226 rectangular glass TLC developing tank with its lid (121 mm side to side, 83 mm front to back, 108 mm tall; glass about 3 mm, so about 115 x 77 mm inside), its long sides facing the robot, centred at (250, -160), with 44 mL of water, 5 mm deep, as the solvent; its flat glass lid (about 125 x 87 x 4 mm) lies flat on the bench at (135, -250). A 75 mm plate standing on the tank's floor and resting on its back wall leans about asin(d / 75) from vertical, d being how far its bottom edge stands from the wall; up to 37 degrees its baseline stays 3 mm above 5 mm of water. Rack, vial block and bar are taped down; the tank stands free inside a tape outline of its footprint. Nothing else is on the bench; the layout is the same every trial. A phone on a stand outside the arms' reach films the plate for scoring; it is not a robot input.
scoring: Twelve checks, 1/12 each. A phone on a stand outside the arms' reach films the plate on its bar throughout, zoomed so the plate fills the frame: (a) and (b) are read from its last frame before the plate is lifted, against the 6 mm tick spacing, because the spots start to move once the plate is in the water; (c) with a 10x loupe on the dried plate after the trial; (d) to (f) from a side photo of the tank with a ruler and a protractor; the rest from the trial video. Per lane: (a) one spot of its own sample covers the tick's crossing with the baseline; (b) the spot is at most 3 mm across (half the tick spacing); (c) no bare glass longer than 1 mm within 3 mm of the tick; (b) and (c) count only with (a). Plate: (d) it stands in the tank right way up, its bottom edge in the water, the baseline at least 3 mm above the water; (e) it rests against the tank's back wall with its spotted face away from the wall (a plate facing the wall fails), at most 35 degrees from vertical; (f) the lid rests on the rim, centred within 6 mm, level within 4 degrees and square to the tank within 8 degrees; (e) and (f) count only with (d). 1.0 also needs all three spotters standing back in rack holes and both grippers 50 mm clear of the tank and its lid; otherwise at most 11/12. Score 0 if a spotter breaks or is dropped (more than 60 degrees from upright with no gripper holding it, or its tip on the bench outside the rack and vials), the plate is dropped (face down on the bench, where the spots smear, or off the bench; lying face up is not a zero), the baseline goes under the water, or the tank is tipped past 10 degrees or pushed more than 5 mm off its outline. The simulated trial ends 1 s after 1.0, at a zero, or at the run limit; a real trial ends when both arms are back and still for 1 s, at a zero, or at the run limit.
reset_notes: The plate is used up: take a new one each trial and pencil its baseline and ticks through a template (a card with the baseline and the three tick positions cut out). Empty, dry and refill the tank to 5 mm (44 mL), stand it back inside its tape outline and lay its lid back on its mark; rinse the three spotters with water, blow them dry and stand them in their holes; top each vial up to 1 mL from its stock; check the finger cots for dye or glass and replace them; a broken spotter is replaced and its glass cleared before the next trial. Wipe up any spilt water or dye with paper towels and dry the bench and the robot before the next trial. Pick up broken glass with tweezers or a brush into a broken-glass box; wear safety glasses at the bench.
fidelity: No liquid or silica is simulated. A spotter fills after its tip stays 2 mm under a sample for 0.25 s; a spot forms only with tip contact at 0.05 to 1.0 N held 0.1 s, growing as sqrt(1 + 16 t) mm with contact time; over 1 N for 0.1 s or 1 mm of sliding gouges; over 3 N on a spotter from anything but the pads breaks it. Thresholds are estimates. Spotters are 1.5 mm square rods of 2 g (real 0.26 g); the plate is a 2.25 mm box; the foam rack is rigid; bodies move only by contact.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (4,770 of 4,800 steps; lifted capillary 1 from its rack, then it slipped from the grip and tipped over: dropped, scored 0); demo: 1.0 in Isaac Sim (3,033 of 4,800 steps; two runs of the final code with byte-identical scorer traces; see README)
